name: Cumbria Chamber of Commerce
what: The Employer Representative Body that leads Cumbria's LSIP, working with employers, colleges and councils across the county.
why_contact: This is the organisation that wrote the LSIP by asking hundreds of local employers what skills they need.

name: Cumbria Combined Authority
what: The new strategic authority for Cumbria, established in February 2026, taking the lead on transport, skills and employment.
why_contact: They will help decide how skills funding is spent locally, based on what the LSIP says employers need.

name: Cumberland Council
what: One of Cumbria's two unitary councils, covering Carlisle, Copeland and Allerdale, with its own economic growth and business support pages.
why_contact: Their business support pages show how the council backs local jobs and employers in your part of Cumbria.

name: Westmorland and Furness Council
what: Cumbria's other unitary council, covering South Lakeland, Eden and Barrow-in-Furness, with its own economic growth strategy.
why_contact: Their business and economy pages show what's happening for jobs and skills around Kendal, Barrow and the Lakes.

name: Cumbria Growth Hub
what: Cumbria's Growth Hub, offering free advice, training and funding support to businesses across the county.
why_contact: If you want to see how local businesses get help to grow (and the jobs that creates), this is where they turn.

name: Cumbria Careers Hub
what: The local Careers Hub, funded by the Careers & Enterprise Company, linking schools and colleges with employers.
why_contact: They run careers events like Cumbria Careers Day, work experience and employer talks in schools and colleges.

name: University of Cumbria
what: A university with campuses in Carlisle, Ambleside, Lancaster and Barrow-in-Furness, offering degrees in business, health, education and engineering.
why_contact: A good option if you want to study close to home, including degree apprenticeships linked to local employers.

name: Kendal College
what: An FE college in Kendal offering A levels, T Levels and apprenticeships, including land-based courses developed with LANSS.
why_contact: Worth checking if you're interested in apprenticeships, especially in engineering or land-based careers.

name: Carlisle College
what: An FE college in Carlisle offering 16-18 courses, apprenticeships and adult learning, with strong hospitality and chef training facilities.
why_contact: A good place to check for chef training, apprenticeships and other courses linked to Cumbria's priority sectors.

name: LANSS (Land & Nature Skills Service)
what: A Cumbria-wide service connecting learners, employers and training providers in farming, forestry and conservation careers.
why_contact: If you're curious about a career working outdoors with land and nature, this is the best place to start looking.
